description:
FILED s473t6d (Opus, 2026-09-20) by #1501 round 11 (CHECK 2 on t/op/sprintf.t).

TWO measured facts, one conversion family.

(a) A `version` OBJECT as the argument of `%vd` / `%vx` / `%v.3d` / `%0*v*d`.
    perl formats the version's own components; PCL either prints ` MISSING`
    (the object contributes no argument at all) or formats the ORDINALS OF
    ITS STRINGIFICATION:

        sprintf "%vd", version::qv("1.2.3")    perl 1.2.3    PCL  MISSING
        sprintf "%vd", version->new("1.2")     perl 1.2      PCL 49.46.50
        sprintf "%vx", version::qv("1.20.300") perl 1.14.12c PCL  MISSING

    49/46/50 are the code points of "1", "." and "2" -- `%vd` applied to the
    STRING the object stringifies to.  Which of the two answers appears
    depends on the spelling, so the object is reaching the formatter in two
    different shapes.

(b) The `+` flag on a vector conversion applies to the FIRST component only:

        sprintf "%+-v3d", "\01\02\03"          perl "+1 .2  .3  "
                                               PCL  "+1 .+2 .+3 "
        sprintf "%+-v*d", 3, "\01\02\03"       same divergence

ROWS: baselines/perl-suite-fails.tsv op/sprintf.t 147 148 149 150 151 152 155
158 169 441 442 (half a) and 157 165 (half b).

SHAPE: (b) is one line in the vector loop -- apply the sign flag to component
0 only.  (a) needs the argument to arrive as the version object (probe what
`%vd`'s argument reader does with a blessed operand before assuming it is
`lib/version.pm`'s problem; the ` MISSING` answer says the reader dropped it,
which is a formatter fact, not a module one).
subject: the `%v` VECTOR conversion family: a `version` object contributes NO argument, and `%+-v3d` signs EVERY component (13 rows of t/op/sprintf.t)
